title: Pixel-Level Transformers in Remote Sensing: A Canopy Height Case Study
abstract: arXiv:2609.37809v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Predicting canopy height from medium-resolution satellite imagery is a common and scalable approach for assessing the condition of the world's forests, which play a crucial role in climate change mitigation. While Transformer-based architectures have shown strong performance in many domains, their straightforward application to dense (i.e., pixel-level) regression tasks often yields suboptimal results. In particular, the patch size has a crucial impact on the model performance. In this work, we consider pixel-level attention schemes and show that the resulting models generally outperform those relying on larger patch sizes. However, pixel-level attention can be a prohibitively resource-intensive operation. translated_title: 遥感中的像素级Transformer：树冠高度案例研究
translated_abstract: 从中等分辨率卫星影像预测树冠高度是评估全球森林状况的一种常见且可扩展的方法，而森林在减缓气候变化方面发挥着至关重要的作用。尽管基于Transformer的架构在许多领域都展现出强大的性能，但将其直接应用于密集（即像素级）回归任务往往会产生次优结果。特别是，patch大小对模型性能有着至关重要的影响。在这项工作中，我们研究了像素级注意力机制，并表明由此得到的模型通常优于依赖较大patch大小的模型。然而，像素级注意力可能是一种极其消耗资源的操作。为此，我们使用高效的注意力变体开展了广泛的实验研究，以确定预测质量与资源需求之间的有利权衡，从而促进所提出方法的实际部署。
tldr: 本文以树冠高度预测为案例，证明像素级Transformer注意力机制优于大patch方案，并通过高效注意力变体的实验找到了预测质量与计算资源需求之间的最佳权衡，促进了该方法的实际部署。
en_tdlr: Using canopy height prediction as a case study, this paper demonstrates that pixel-level attention in Transformers outperforms larger patch sizes, and identifies efficient attention variants that achieve favorable trade-offs between prediction quality and resource requirements for practical deployment.
